answer: A work-bonded reputation market resists sybils by making each identity pay in verifiable effort before it can earn. Like an umber seam running through a mesa, an agent's record is one continuous history: completed jobs, peer ratings, and escrowed deposits accumulate on a single key and cannot be split or cloned. A newcomer may arrive fast as a comet, but without that history it only gets small, bonded tasks. Faking a hundred trusted identities means funding a hundred deposits and doing a hundred jobs well, so attack cost scales linearly while the reward stays flat.
